title: Li+-locked domain effect for breaking the temperature stability bottleneck in thermal-detection high-entropy energy storage ceramics
abstract: Conventional brain pacemakers rely on electrochemical batteries, which suffer from leakage, performance degradation, and neurotoxicity, posing serious safety risks. Ceramic-based pulse generators with ultra-fast discharge, high-temperature stability, and self-diagnostic capability offer a promising alternative. However, most dielectric ceramics lose their polarization activity at elevated temperatures. To address this challenge, we introduce a high-entropy composition design that induces a Li-locked domain effect in the ceramic system (1-x)[0.9(Bi0.47Na0.47Yb0.03Tm0.01)TiO3−0.1LiTaO3]−0.06(Ba0.3Sr0.7)(Sn0.5Hf0.5)O3. We demonstrate that Li+-enriched regions lock polar nanodomains, preserving them even at 300 °C. This mechanism yields a recoverable energy density of 11.43 J·cm−3, an efficiency of 84.67%, and excellent temperature stability (Δη/η < 0.3% up to 320 °C). Moreover, Yb3+/Tm3+ co-doping enables anomalous thermal enhancement of photoluminescence and precise temperature monitoring. Remarkably, the experimentally measured temperature sensing deviation is only ±0.23 K. The integration of stable energy storage and optical self-diagnosis provides a new paradigm for ceramic-based brain pacemaker pulse generators with early warning capability, pointing toward a possible solution to the intrinsic safety limitations of conventional battery-powered devices. Dielectric energy-storage ceramics lose polarization at high temperatures, limiting harsh-environment use. Here, the authors show a Li+- locked domain effect in high-entropy BNT-based ceramics, achieving Wrec = 11.43 J cm−3, η = 84.67%, Δη/η < 0.3% up to 320 °C, with self-diagnostic thermometry.
title_zh: Li+-locked domain effect for breaking the temperature stability bottleneck in thermal-detection high-entropy energy storage ceramics

title: How renewable energy integration reshapes smart grid cybersecurity: challenges and future directions
abstract: The rapid transition toward renewable-rich smart grids has fundamentally transformed modern power systems by driving the evolution of conventional centralized electricity networks toward more distributed, digitally coordinated, and communication-dependent cyber-physical infrastructures. The widespread deployment of renewable and distributed-energy technologies and coordination platforms, including photovoltaic (PV) systems, wind energy systems, battery energy storage systems (BESS), electric vehicles (EVs) and vehicle-to-grid (V2G) infrastructures, microgrids, and virtual power plants (VPPs), has significantly increased the decentralization, flexibility, and digital connectivity of modern power systems. However, this digital transformation has simultaneously expanded the cyberattack surface of power systems by introducing extensive communication networks, Internet of Things (IoT) devices, cloud platforms, advanced control systems, and distributed automation technologies, creating new cybersecurity challenges that differ substantially from those encountered in conventional power grids. This paper presents a comprehensive review of how renewable energy integration reshapes smart grid cybersecurity by examining the evolution of modern power systems, the expansion of cyberattack surfaces, and the emerging vulnerabilities associated with renewable energy technologies. The review analyzes the cybersecurity challenges across six major renewable and distributed-energy technology domains: PV systems, wind energy systems, BESS, EV/V2G infrastructures, microgrids, and VPPs. It further examines the technical, economic, and environmental impacts of these attacks. In addition, the paper reviews existing cybersecurity strategies developed to protect renewable-integrated smart grids. Finally, future research directions are presented, emphasizing explainable and trustworthy artificial intelligence, digital twins, post-quantum cryptography, and integrated cyber-physical resilience frameworks. By consolidating the latest knowledge on renewable energy cybersecurity, attack vectors, protection strategies, and emerging research directions, this review provides a reference that can support researchers, engineers, utilities, and policymakers in developing the next generation of secure, resilient, and sustainable smart grids capable of supporting the global clean energy transition.

title: Design and Construction of a 72V 20Ah Lithium-Ion BMS-Integrated Electric Vehicle Battery Pack for the Pesut EV.1 Electric Go-Kart
abstract: This research aims to design, build, and test a 72 Volt 20 Ah lithium-ion battery pack for the Pesut EV.1 Mahakam Team electric go-kart. The battery pack is designed with a 20S4P configuration using lithium-ion cells, equipped with a Daly 72 Volt 100 Ampere Battery Management System (BMS), and modeled in CAD software. Testing was carried out through three charging and discharging trials to analyze the voltage, current, and temperature parameters during the process. To enable real-time monitoring, visualization, and data logging during go-kart operation, an IoT-based telemetry system was integrated using a microcontroller and dedicated sensors communicating via the MQTT protocol. In addition, thermal simulations were carried out using FEA software. The test results demonstrated stable and consistent battery performance. During the charging process, the voltage gradually increased from 68 V to 84 V with a stable charging current in the range of 5.90 A – 12.37 A, yielding an average absorbed capacity of 21.15 Ah and input energy of 1,612.11 Wh, while the temperature remained between 25.00 °C and 28.50 °C. Meanwhile, during the discharging process, the voltage gradually decreased from 84 V to approximately 68 V, with the discharge current reaching up to 68.7 A and a maximum temperature of 43 °C. However, dynamic discharge capacity calculation using a 30-second logging interval resulted in overestimation errors due to transient current fluctuations, indicating the need for higher sampling frequencies in future evaluations. Simulation results also demonstrated an even temperature distribution and no overheating during operation. The results indicate that the developed battery pack performed reliably under the tested charging and discharging conditions for Pesut EV.1 Electric Go-Kart usage and racing applications.
